lessons.title: Matrix Representation and Traversal
lessons.concept: A matrix (2D array) is a collection of elements arranged in rows and columns. Elements are accessed using row and column indices (commonly 0-based). Traversal patterns include row-wise, column-wise, and diagonal traversals depending on the problem.
lessons.formula: For matrix with R rows and C columns: element at (i,j) where 0 <= i < R, 0 <= j < C. Row-wise: for i in rows: for j in cols. Column-wise: for j in cols: for i in rows.
lessons.worked_example: Matrix [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] has 2 rows, 3 cols. Row-wise traversal visits 1,2,3,4,5,6. Element at (1,2) is 6 (0-based).
mistakes: Out-of-bounds access when loop limits are incorrect
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Common Matrix Operations
lessons.concept: Basic operations include transpose (swap rows and columns), searching, summing rows/columns, and boundary/spiral traversal patterns. Transpose of an R x C matrix becomes C x R with element (i,j) mapped to (j,i).
lessons.formula: Transpose: T[j][i] = M[i][j]. For square matrix in-place transpose swaps M[i][j] with M[j][i] for j > i. Boundary traversal visits top row, right column, bottom row, left column in order.
mistakes: Trying in-place transpose on non-square matrix without proper storage
Visiting corner elements twice in boundary traversal
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Matrix Search and Patterns
lessons.concept: Some problems exploit matrix properties for efficient search. For example, in a matrix where each row and column is sorted, searching can be done by starting at a corner and eliminating a row or column at each step. Other problems involve rotations or layer-wise processing.
lessons.formula: Sorted row/col matrix search (ascending): start at top-right; if value > target move left, if value < target move down (O(R+C)). 90-degree rotation (square) often done by transpose + reverse rows (or layer cycles).
lessons.worked_example: In [[1,4,7],[2,5,8],[3,6,9]] to find 5: start at 7 (>5 move left to 4, <5 move down to 5) found.
mistakes: Applying sorted-matrix search technique to unsorted matrices
Modifying matrix while still needing original values
